name: Married Put
summary: Buy the shares and the protective put at the same moment, in one order, so the downside is capped from the first tick and the tax lot is matched.

legs.strike_rule: ATM to 5% OTM (0.40-0.50 delta) for a tight floor

when_to_use: Initiating a new, higher-risk long (a breakout, a small cap, an earnings run-up) where the maximum loss must be known in advance. Also used when the system wants share exposure but cannot tolerate gap risk.
entry_rules: Submit the shares and put together as one combined order where possible; otherwise buy the put FIRST, then the shares.
Put strike chosen so max loss <= 1.5% of account equity for the whole unit.
Require IV Rank <= 45; married puts in high IV are a poor value - use a collar instead.
Premium <= 5% of share notional for a 90+ DTE put.
management_rules: Roll the put up and out once the shares are up more than the put premium, converting paper gains into a raised floor.
At DTE < 30, roll out or close the unit.
If IV Rank climbs above 65 while holding, sell a call against the shares to convert the married put into a collar and recover hedge cost.
exit_rules: HARD: never let the put auto-exercise. If ITM, close it by 15:30 ET on expiration day and decide about the shares separately.
Exit the unit when the thesis completes (target reached) by selling shares and put together.
If the shares gap below the strike, the unit's loss is already capped - exit on schedule rather than panicking.
assignment_risk: No short leg; no assignment risk. Unwanted auto-exercise of the ITM long put is the only mechanical hazard, and it liquidates the shares at the strike.
buying_power: Share cost plus put premium, both in cash.
liquidity_needs: OI >= 250; longer-dated strikes on liquid names only.
common_mistakes: Paying for a 180-day ATM put on a low-vol name and guaranteeing underperformance; treating the married put as free insurance rather than a real drag of 4-8% annually.
family: Stock/ETF Shares Combined With Options (covered writes, protective hedges, collars, synthetics, repairs, conversions)
